tei:titleStmt.tei:title: חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה
Ḥanaiah, Mishael, and Azariah — a piyyuṭ for the Seder Meturgeman of Shavuot

tei:div.tei:head: Ḥanaiah, Mishael, and Azariah — a piyyuṭ for the Seder Meturgeman of Shavuot

tei:lg.tei:l: Ḥananiah, Mishael, and Azariah proclaimed the name of the blessed Holy One
before the eyes of all life, when the dwarf charged them and thus said to them:
Come, bow down to my image, palm-fronds! — said the dwarf.
Understand what I did to you when You were in Ẓion. — said the dwarf.
I set waste in the baldachin of your Master! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
In our Parent above we trust. — said Hanaiah.
In Them we have trusted from our youth. — said Mishael.
We would burn in the fire rather than deny Them. — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
You are causing yourselves to be burned! — said the dwarf.
Your bodies will be made ash in the fiery oven. — said the dwarf.
If your God has strength and dynamism, let Them save you! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
Reverence for your image is not in our heart! — said Hanaiah.
The form of an image we do not worship! — said Mishael.
Know that our Patron is watching over you! — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
How you are deniers, not to bow down to my image! — said the dwarf.
Now you will bow before my effigy, and if not, burn! — said the dwarf.
Hey, you have to know you will bow even against your will! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
And what would we say to the Dweller in heaven? — said Hanaiah.
And They reveal mysteries and secrets! — said Mishael.
And with Them are beams of light, and They reveal darkness! — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
I am throwing you, bound, into the fiery furnace! — said the dwarf.
I am angry at you that you rebel against me and my image! — said the dwarf.
When you hear the sound of the horn, bow before my image! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
The Living and Enduring One is our Patron! — said Hanaiah.
Shame on the children who deny their Parent! — said Mishael.
Far be it for us to deny “We will do and hear!” — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
I have butchered and slaughtered Ẓion’s fledglings! — said the dwarf.
Fast and roaring was I like a lion in the baldachin of your Master! — said the dwarf.
I tossed aside the heads of your babies, and none saved them! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
Woe betide you, dwarf, how you blaspheme! — said Hanaiah.
Learn from Pharaoh who was before you. — said Mishael.
Unique is our God who watches over us! — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
All the earth’s residents are conquered and struck dumb by me! — said the dwarf.
All my senators appear before my image and not a man rebels! — said the dwarf.
How stiff-necked are you not to bow to my image! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
We need not answer you on this matter. — said Hanaiah.
We have no desire in a god that a human formed. — said Mishael.
To our God, who passed us through the sea on dry land, we worship and bow. — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
Meshach, Shadrach, and Abednego! — said the dwarf.
From the Teaching of Moses look and consider! — said the dwarf.
You are scattered and worshipped something secret, not great! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
We are careful to recall the covenants. — said Hanaiah.
Our vow was to guard the word of a king. — said Mishael.
We pay per-capita taxes, property-taxes, and damages! — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
You filled your land with images belonging to apostates from the Jews! — said the dwarf.
Pigments you formed on the walls, images of Chaldeans! — said the dwarf.
Now you think to render nothingness to my image? — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
Upon this, we need not answer you. — said Hanaiah.
The Highest can save us from your hand and from the erupting oven. — said Mishael.
Whether They act or not, Their name we will exalt aflame. — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
You multiplied mobs of cults to nothingness and waste! — said the dwarf.
I’m spreading a curtain for you — take notes and write — said the dwarf.
That you will keep my orders, returing in thirty days. — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
The first note: “If we forget our God’s name!” — said Hanaiah.
The second letter inscribed: “Wouldn’t God investigate this?” — said Mishael.
Clearly written: “For You we are killed!” — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
“Gather them and give them to a child to read them aloud!” — ordered the dwarf.
He read them publicly, before all the nations and all the army.
His face’s appearance changed in roaring frothing rage.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
Like a cricket, flask, and dog you are to be shamed! — said Hanaiah.
We wish the greatness of the holy Watcher to be seen! — said Mishael.
Burn us at the seventh level, as hot as can be! — said Azariah.
We will not deny “Do not have for yourselves!” — shouted those three.
The former part of Jeremiah’s verse you’ve settled to cancel. — said the dwarf.
I wish to fulfill the latter, since you rebelliously provoked me. — said the dwarf.
Call the men in the army to force them and cast them into the oven! — said the dwarf.
We have a Patron whose name is “Neither slumbers nor sleeps!” — shouted those three.
The endangered great ones were unchanged in mantle, coat, and cap.
They were thrown into the fiery oven, but were undamaged by injury.
The smell of fire didn’t come upon them — heat did not rule their bodies.
The Mighty Sovereign sent the angel that flies through the world in two flights.
He turned it up on the outside and cooled it on the inside, and did miracles within miracles.
Six were done on that very day that the well-born ones were tested.
The dwarf was terrified and rose in panic when he saw four unbound and walking.
“Go and take out the servants of the highest God, Sovereign, Soveriegn of sovereigns!
Tell of Their wonders and signs, for great are Their victories in the provinces’ cities!”
Praise before the Cause, all peoples! — said Hanaiah.
Praise Them, all nations! — said Mishael.
For great over us is Their goodness in heaven — said Azariah.
And the truth of the Cause is eternal! — said Gabriel.
Content are the righteous who trust in the name of the blessed Holy One.
For in their plaudits and their praises the ministering angels rush.
And in the future, within from them, before the Presence they dwell in the precincts.

tei:note.tei:p: Nebuchadnezzar, based on an interpretation of Daniel 4:14’s “the lowest of men.”
These first two lines, found in most if not all medieval Ashkenazi manuscripts, are not found in the original Byzantine-era piyyuṭ (as compiled by Sokoloff and Yahalom, SYAP 13).
A reference to the three youths, who remained tall instead of bending over See Targum Song of Songs 7:9.
Psalm 121:4. Many manuscripts do not say “nor sleeps” and just read “Does Not Slumber!”
i.e. the second commandment, pluralized. Some texts re-singularize the Aramaic to “Do not have for yourself.”
Some manuscripts read, “the God”
Some manuscripts add “pipe”
Exodus 24:7
Some manuscripts read “All I say of you is that you are free.”
Some manuscripts read “kneel and bow”
Some manuscripts read “Doomed are you for your haughty spirits”
A direct quote from Daniel 3:16. Some manuscripts read “We are not watching out for you or for your image.”
Some manuscripts read “portion”
Some manuscripts read “cast”
Some manuscripts read “As we sang at the sea, we are of ‘this, our God!’” referring to Exodus 15:2.
The original anonymous text ends here.

The Babylonian names given to the three as part of the process of forced assimilation in Daniel 1:7. Hananiah is Shadrach, Mishael is Meshach, and Azariah is Abednego. Though chapter 3 of Daniel almost exclusively uses these Babylonian names, and thus Christians often refer to the three as “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego,” Jewish texts generally use the Hebrew names.
According to Leviticus Rabbah 33:6, Nebuchadnezzar cited Deuteronomy 4:28 as a proof text: “There you will serve gods, the work of human hand.”

i.e. incorporeal. An ancient canard against the Jews, less common now that monotheism is much more prominent worldwide, is that we’re all secretly atheists because we don’t know what our God looks like.
According to Leviticus Rabbah 33:6, the three responded to the citation of Deuteronomy 4:28 by saying it referred to obeying kings in exile, since kings are treated “like gods.”

Each of the three notes cites one of the verses from Psalms 44:21–23.
Leviticus Rabbah 33:6 compares Nebuchadnezzar’s name to a barking [navaḥ] dog, an inflating flask [kad], and a chirping [natsar] cricket.
Find Daniel 4:10
Referring to Jeremiah 27:8’s warning about those who refuse to obey Nebuchadnezzar.
A direct quote from Daniel 2:27
Gabriel. Find Bavli Berakhot 4b
A reference to Pesaḥim 118a-b

Sanhedrin 92b. According to the passage, the six miracles were: the furnace rose from the ground, the furnace was breached, the limestone dissolved, the image fell on its face, four monarchies were burned, and Ezekiel revived the dead in the Dura Valley.
There might be an implied refrain of “— said the dwarf” for these two lines, but to my knowledge it is unattested.
An Aramaic translation of Psalms 117 in its entirety. The word “in heaven” is added for the sake of the rhyme.
The angels above don’t begin their song until Israel below does. Ḥullin 91b
i.e. in the innermost part of the precincts, more so than the angels. Some manuscripts amend this odd phrasing to “in their number”
